Order Sheet  IA-1 of 2024  In Re:
 CRA No. 788 of 2024  Chiranjivi Tandon S/o Kejuram Tandon, Aged About 24 Years R/
o Village  Matiya, P.S. Ranchirai, District- Balod, Chhattisgarh.

... Appellant  versus  State Of Chhattisgarh Through-, S.H.O. Police Station Ranchirai,
 District- Balod, ( C.G.) ...Respondent (Cause title is taken from the CIS)

By the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 10.04.2024 (Annexure A1), passed by the learned First Additional Session Judge/In-charge FTS, Balod, District-Balod, Chhattisgarh in ST- 44 of 2019, appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under with default stipulation :
Cra 788 of 2024 Conviction Sentence Under Section 450 of the RI for 10 years, and fine IPC amount of Rs.1,000/-
Under Section 376(2)(L) of Imprisonment for life lthe IPC (meaning thereby tillthe rest of the natural life of that person) and find amount of Rs.1,000/-

All sentences to run  concurrently Heard Shri Sudhanshu Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the appellant and Shri MK Jain, PL for the State on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (IA-1 of 2024).
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the case and there is no evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of the offence.

It is further argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that trial Court has not appreciated the evidence in a proper way, as the complainant has not produced the disability certificate during the investigation, when she was examined Cra 788 of 2024 before the trial Court, but the same has been produced for evidence after lapse of two years.
FSL report is also not correct as the articles for FSL examination were sent for their examination after lapse of one month of the incident.

being a major lady, aged about 20 years, is a consenting party.
During trial, he was on bail and not misused the liberty.
Appellant is in jail from 10.04.2024 and disposal of this appeal may take some time, hence the appellant may be released on bail.
Learned State counsel though opposes the bail application but does not dispute the fact regarding production of evidence at a later stage.
Trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellant only after appreciation of evidence available before it.
Hence the appellant is not entitled for bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, also considering the fact that prosecutrix is a major lady aged about Cra 788 of 2024 20 years, her examination-in-chief was recorded on 11.12.2019, whereas, again her evidence was recorded on 10.08.2021, after about two years, whereby her disability certificate was produced regarding her mental status, and subsequently, charge under Section 376(2)(L) has been framed, against the appellant, during trial he was on bail, the appellant is in jail since 10.04.2024, and hearing of this appeal would take some more time, without commenting anything on merit, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellant by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

He shall be released on bail on his executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety of the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 25th February, 2025.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to Cra 788 of 2024 him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, bail application (IA-1 of 2024) filed on behalf of the appellant- Chiranjivi Tandon, s/o Kejuram, is allowed.
Let the matter be listed for final hearing in due course.

Sd/- Sd/-d/-
 Sd/ (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) (Ramesh Sinha)
